Slug Algorithm -- reference shaders
MIT OR Apache-2.0 (dual; MIT chosen and vendored here as LICENSE)
https://github.com/EricLengyel/Slug
author: Eric Lengyel, Terathon Software

vendored v3823. NO CODE FROM THE UPSTREAM REPOSITORY IS SHIPPED IN THIS DIRECTORY.

The upstream repository contains exactly two files of substance, SlugVertexShader.hlsl and
SlugPixelShader.hlsl. Both are HLSL and this engine is WebGL2, so they were PORTED rather than
vendored: the GLSL ES 3.00 translation lives in text/slugShader.js, and text/slugFont.js,
text/slugAtlas.js and text/slugText.js are original work implementing the data structures the
shaders read. This directory therefore carries the licence and this record and nothing else,
because there is no upstream artefact to keep in sync.

ATTRIBUTION IS A LICENCE CONDITION, NOT A COURTESY. The upstream README states it plainly: the
code may be used freely by anyone for any purpose and the patent has been dedicated to the public
domain, but anyone distributing software that uses it IS REQUIRED to give credit. The string that
satisfies that is exported as SLUG_NOTICE from text/slugShader.js so a build step can emit it, it
is reproduced in the header of every ported file, and it is repeated here:

    Slug shader code Copyright 2017 by Eric Lengyel. Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0.
    https://github.com/EricLengyel/Slug

PATENT. Slug was patented and the patent has been dedicated to the public domain by its author.
That is the reason this integration exists at all -- the algorithm was commercial-licence-only for
most of its life, and an engine could not have shipped it. Anyone auditing this dependency should
confirm the dedication still stands rather than taking this file's word for it.

The core algorithm is described in:
    Eric Lengyel, "GPU-Centered Font Rendering Directly from Glyph Outlines",
    Journal of Computer Graphics Techniques, Vol. 6, No. 2, 2017.
    https://jcgt.org/published/0006/02/02/
Changes since publication are catalogued at https://terathon.com/blog/decade-slug.html

WHAT THE PORT CHANGED, so a future reader diffing against upstream is not surprised:
  - HLSL intrinsics to their GLSL equivalents (asuint, saturate, frac, Load, nointerpolation).
  - The two packed integer words arrive as a genuine uvec2 attribute through vertexAttribIPointer
    instead of being bit-cast out of a float4, because WebGL2 has an integer attribute path and
    D3D9-era vertex declarations did not. The BIT LAYOUT is unchanged.
  - kLogBandTextureWidth is injected rather than hardcoded at 12, because WebGL2 guarantees only a
    2048 texel MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE while the reference assumes 4096.
Nothing else. The port is otherwise line-for-line and is meant to stay diffable by eye.
